title: Embeddings throughput throttle — comm draft & all‑hands crib
content:
Purpose:
This is a quick internal comms draft + all-hands crib for a short, controlled throttle of embeddings throughput in NA region to mitigate a memory growth issue observed in the embeddings worker pool (ENG-4821). Use this as a working playbook — lots of TODOs below.

TL;DR (for execs):
- We will temporarily cap per-customer embeddings throughput in us-west/us-east for a 48–72 hour window starting 2026-03-15 00:00 UTC to keep the fleet stable while we roll a hotfix.
- Impact: ~3–8% latency increase for bursty jobs; large batch jobs may be enqueued/delayed. Priority customers get exception paths (see checklist).
- Why: deterministic memory growth under heavy prefix reuse + large batch sizes causing OOMs in a subset of instances; mitigation buys time for fix and controlled rollout.
- Ask from all: unify talking points, send one customer-facing blast + per-key-account outreach, prepare SRE runbook and on-call backup.

Audience:
- All-hands: engineering, product, CS, solutions eng, sales ops, support.
- External: affected customers (automated email + account teams), public status page update.

Key messages (single-sentence versions):
- We discovered abnormal memory growth in a subset of embeddings workers under certain batch/prefix patterns. To protect stability, we are temporarily capping throughput while we deploy a targeted fix.
- This is limited in time and scope; we expect normal behavior to resume after verification.
- We will proactively contact customers with heavy batch jobs and offer escalations.

Suggested CEO/VP Eng talking points (for 60s):
- Prep: keep it calm and technical-simple.
- "We discovered a specific memory-growth pattern in our embeddings pipeline that could, in edge conditions, impact serving reliability. We've implemented a temporary cap on throughput to protect customers and give the team time to safely deploy a fix. We’re prioritizing high-SLA customers for exception handling and will post regular status updates."

Ops playbook (short):
- 03/15 00:00 UTC: Activate throttle policy in NA routing layer (policy id: EMB-TEMP-0326).
- 00:00–04:00 UTC: Run smoke tests on canary cohort (region canaries + 10 internal test orgs).
- 04:00–48:00 UTC: Monitor errored requests, OOMs, tail latency, and memory curves (dashboards: Embeddings > memory-growth > embargoed).
- 24:00 UTC: If OOMs <= baseline and mem slopes flatten, begin controlled rollback in batches of 20% capacity per 6h.
- 72:00 UTC: Target full rollback if rollout metrics meet SLOs.

Customer-facing short message (for email/status page):
- Subject: Short, temporary change to embeddings throughput to improve stability
- Body (short): "We are temporarily limiting embeddings throughput in US regions to address an internal memory-growth issue affecting stability. Most customers will see little or no impact. If your workflows include very large batched embedding jobs, you may experience delays; your account team will reach out if we detect high-impact usage. We expect normal service to return within ~72 hours. We’ll post updates to status.redwood.ai and directly to affected accounts."

Anticipated Q&A (rough):
- Q: Will data or models be affected?
  A: No — no data loss and no model changes. This is a serving-layer throughput mitigation.
- Q: Which customers are affected?
  A: Customers with sustained, very large batched embedding jobs in NA. We’ll surface a list to account teams (see `linked_artifacts`).
- Q: Why not fix in prod immediately?
  A: The fix requires a coordinated, kernel-level memory management change and staged rollout to avoid wider regressions. The throttle reduces risk while we validate.
- Q: What are the rollback conditions?
  A: No new OOMs for 24h across canaries, stable memory slope, tail latency within 10% of baseline, and SRE sign-off.

Escalation + contact matrix (who speaks to whom):
- Account escalations: Ravi P (primary), Mikaela O (backup).
- Technical press / public: VP Eng (draft only) + comms.
- Status updates: triage channel #ops-embeddings (notify @SRE-oncall, @eng-embeddings).

Monitoring & dashboards (where to look):
- Dash: Embeddings > mem-growth > per-instance (internal dash id EMB-MEM-23)
- Logs: cloud-logs/embeddings/oom (alert: OOM-embeddings-high)
- Traces: Sampling 1% of embedding batch traces; correlate with prefix reuse tag.

Checklists (TODOs, many are owner-tagged):
- [ ] Finalize customer email (owner: Aria) — include account teams list by 03/13 EOD.
- [ ] Post status.redwood.ai short update (owner: Support) — 03/15 00:05 UTC scheduled.
- [ ] Prepare rollback playbook snippet for SRE runbook (owner: SRE lead).
- [ ] Coordinate exception list for priority customers (owner: Ravi).
- [ ] Validate canary smoke tests (owner: Mikaela).
- [ ] PR approval for hotfix (runtime PR #974) and gatekeeper sign-off for deploy windows.

Notes to self (scratch, keep):
- Customers likely to call: top-10 embeddings spenders + 5 large batch customers we flagged earlier (see spreadsheet in Confluence link).
- Need to pair with product to ensure optimize suggestions UI doesn't recommend large batch sizes while throttle active.
- Consider one-off quota bump for customers doing critical migrations (manual review).

Open questions (resolve before send):
- A1: Exact throttle algorithm: global token/s per org vs per-instance concurrency cap? (SRE input needed)
- A2: Messaging on billing: will customers be charged for queued work? Need Finance answer.
- A3: If hotfix rolls back memory growth but increases cost by X% due to less efficient kernels, how do we communicate?

Slack snippets (short, for channel):
- Ops alert: "Activating embeddings throughput throttle (EMB-TEMP-0326) at 2026-03-15 00:00 UTC. Expect minor delays for large batches. See docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-4821-memory-leak-investigation. Ravi/Mikaela handling account escalations."

Post-mortem anchors (what to capture after):
- Trigger and detection time, root cause hypothesis, fix details and PRs, rollback conditions observed, customer impact list + outreach log, follow-up changes to autoscaling/metrics, and lessons for release gating.

Rough timeline for comms cadence (sample):
- 03/13 EOD: Finalize internal script and list of affected accounts.
- 03/14 12:00 UTC: Exec briefing + dry-run of CEO 60s script.
- 03/15 00:00 UTC: Activate throttle + status page + account emails.
- 03/15 06:00, 03/16 06:00, 03/17 06:00 UTC: Regular ops updates.

Finish notes: this doc is a living scratchpad. Keep it lean — move polished copies to shared_drives/engineering/observability once stable.

-- Aria
